desks.title: Month-end close — day 3, $53k still unexplained
desks.description: Day 3 of a five-day close for a two-entity food distributor: balance sheet reconciliations, the four accounts that don't tie, and the journals waiting on the CFO.
desks.brief:
## Month-end close — day 3 of 5

**Entity** Saltbush Provisions · wholesale food distribution · AU parent + NZ subsidiary
**Flash P&L to Dana (CFO)** @+2d · **Board pack** @+6d
**Materiality** $5,000 per account — payroll liabilities get fixed whatever the size

### Where it stands
Six of eleven balance sheet reconciliations are signed off. Four accounts don't tie, **$53,013 unexplained in total**:
- Inventory — $26,840: cold-store count under the stock system
- Trade creditors — $12,573: one packaging invoice keyed twice
- NZ intercompany — $12,400: freight recharge not booked on the NZ side
- Super payable — $1,200: a salary-sacrifice change accrued by hand as well as through payroll

### Before the flash goes out
- Chiller 2 recounted, and the inventory gap either confirmed or found
- Journals J-0412 and J-0414 approved by Dana; J-0413 is under $5,000 and mine to approve
- NZ agrees the intercompany balance, or the difference is disclosed in the pack

### The number that matters
If all three journals post, the month's result moves by **−$14,210**. Inventory is the only one that could still change that answer.

callout.title: Inventory gap: recount before we book it
callout.body: The cold-store count is $26,840 under the stock system — about 0.6 points of gross margin this month. Recount chiller 2 with Leah at 7am @+1d, and check deliveries received after the count cut-off before anyone writes anything off.

children.label: Freight recharge not booked in NZ
Agree the balance with the NZ team
Which FX rate did NZ use?

blocks.p: Every adjustment for this close, with the evidence behind it. Dana approves anything over $5,000; anything under, I approve and note for her.

ul: Evidence: the supplier statement shows one invoice; AP keyed it twice, two days apart

blocks.p: Dr Super payable $1,200 · Cr Superannuation expense $1,200. The salary-sacrifice change went through payroll and was also accrued by hand. Under $5,000 — approved by me, noted for Dana.
Dr Cost of sales — stock loss $26,840 · Cr Inventory $26,840. **Not posted until the chiller 2 recount** @+1d. The amount may change.
+$11,430 packaging + $1,200 super − $26,840 stock = **−$14,210** to the month's result. No journal on the AU side for intercompany — NZ books the recharge.

notes.title: For Dana's flash pack
notes.body:
- Revenue $4.47m for the month; gross margin 21.8% before any stock write-off, 21.2% after
- The inventory gap is the headline. If the recount confirms it, say so plainly and show the chiller 2 trend for the last three months
- NZ intercompany: if it isn't agreed by @+2d, disclose the $12,400 as an open item rather than force it
- Duplicate invoice: AP is turning on the duplicate invoice-number check in the ledger — worth one line
- Wages accrual ties; it only needs my review tonight

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. Confirm recount crew for 7am
2. Approve J-0413
3. Chase NZ on the freight recharge
4. Review wages accrual
5. Start flash commentary

stickies.title: Rule
stickies.body: Under $5k: note it, don't chase it. Payroll liabilities are the exception — fix them.

desks.title: 13-week cash forecast — Fernhill Joinery over its limit in week 7
desks.description: Advisory work for a joinery client: a 13-week cash forecast, the overdraft breach it shows, and the two levers that fix it before the meeting with the owner.
desks.brief:
## 13-week cash forecast — Fernhill Joinery

**Client** Fernhill Joinery · custom cabinetry and commercial fit-out · 18 staff
**Facility** $100,000 overdraft · **Opening balance** $46,200 in credit
**Meeting with Tama (owner)** @+3d · annual bank review in five weeks

### What the forecast shows
The account goes overdrawn in week 4, when the quarterly BAS ($58,300) and super ($21,400) land together. It **breaches the $100,000 limit in weeks 7 and 8**, bottoming at −$126,300, before Larkspur Constructions' progress claim of $118,800 arrives in week 9.

### Why
- Larkspur paid claims 1–3 between 19 and 24 days late, so claim 4 is modelled in week 9, not week 6 when it falls due
- A $24,000 deposit on the new edgebander is booked for week 5
- Wages run fortnightly at $48,600 and don't move

### What I'll recommend
1. Get Larkspur to pay claim 4 on terms — on its own that keeps Fernhill inside the limit, just
2. Push the edgebander deposit to week 10
3. Ask the bank for a temporary limit increase now, as a backstop, not after the breach

### What it doesn't fix
Over the 13 weeks Fernhill pays out $738,000 and collects $680,000. Timing solves the breach; margin on the commercial jobs is the next conversation.

callout.title: Use both levers, then ask the bank
callout.body: Claim 4 on time keeps the account inside the limit, but with only $5,100 of headroom in week 5. Deferring the edgebander alone still breaches by $2,300 in week 7. Together, the low point is −$70,900 with $29,100 to spare.

table.title: Cash forecast — bank basis, GST inclusive

children.label: On time in week 6 = no breach
Tama calls their CFO, not AP
Will the supplier hold the price?
Payment plan if cash is short

blocks.h3: Cash forecast — what it means and what to do

blocks.p: Prepared for our meeting @+3d. Figures are bank basis and GST inclusive, built from the debtors and creditors listings at today's date and the job schedule you sent.
On current timing the account is overdrawn from week 4 and over the $100,000 limit in weeks 7 and 8, by up to $26,300. It recovers in week 9 when Larkspur's claim 4 arrives.

ol: Call Larkspur's finance lead this week and confirm claim 4 will be paid on its due date in week 6.
Move the edgebander deposit from week 5 to week 10, if the supplier will hold the quoted price.
Ask the bank for a temporary $40,000 limit increase for 12 weeks, with this forecast attached.
Keep lodging the BAS on time. If cash is short, ask for a payment plan rather than lodging late.

ul: No new residential deposits included — anything signed is upside
Wages flat at $48,600 a fortnight, no overtime
Timber and board prices as per the latest supplier quote

notes.title: Questions for Tama before I finalise
notes.body:
- Has Larkspur said anything about claim 4, or are we assuming late again?
- Is the edgebander deposit refundable if we push it?
- Any residential jobs about to sign? A deposit or two would cover the week 7 hole on its own
- Is rent still $9,800 a month, or has the landlord agreed the new terms?
- Who else holds a card on the account — any spend I'm not seeing?

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. Rerun weeks 5–9 with claim 4 on time
2. Draft the advice note
3. Send Tama the questions

stickies.title: Bank
stickies.body: Banks want the forecast before the breach, not after.
